text:
ryan: Heads up — our prod 429 rate jumped for org=acme on /v1/generate ~10:40 UTC, visible on the quotas dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quotas/429s?org=acme :eyes:
ops-bot: ALERT fired: 429-rate-high (org=acme) — 12% 429s over last 5m, monitor id 9876
ryan: Is this quota enforcement (burst) or upstream model errors?
maria: Any config changes last night? routing or routing weights?
alex: Likely per-key burst limits tripping. Quick PromQL to confirm 429 ratio by org:
```
sum by (org)(increase(http_requests_total{code="429"}[5m]))
/ sum by (org)(increase(http_requests_total[5m]))
```
alex: Also slice by `rate_limit_reason` if available — that tells us "burst" vs "global_quota"
sunil: We did a tiny routing tweak 02:30 UTC to prefer model-b for short requests. Could increase short-lived bursts to model-b, might have affected pipelines.
sunil: Rate limiter logs look noisy, will grep for acme:
```
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=rate-limiter -c rate-limiter --since=1h | grep "org=acme"
```
jamie: CS: any ETA to know if customers are impacted broadly? I can message the account if we have root cause and ETA.
alex: Minimal triage runbook (short):
```
1) Open quotas dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quotas) and confirm org-level 429 spike.
2) Check rate_limit_reason tag (burst, org_quota, global) and per-key breakdown.
3) Inspect rate-limiter logs for org token and enforcement events.
4) If per-key burst: temporarily bump burst window for the org via admin API.
5) If system overload: enable fallback to cheaper model or throttle ingress for non-critical routes.
6) Notify CS and set customer-facing message if impact > 5% requests.
```
alex: Example admin API call to bump burst (SRE-only):
```
POST https://admin.redwood.ai/api/v1/quotas/update
{
  "org": "acme",
  "delta_burst": 2000
}
```
sam: oncall: I’ll take it. Increasing acme burst by 2x now and watching for 10m, will rollback if it causes side effects.
sam: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"org":"acme","burst":2000}' https://admin.redwood.ai/api/v1/quotas/update` :white_check_mark:
ryan: Thanks — can we improve the alert to split by `rate_limit.reason` and surface the top offending orgs in the alert subject? Right now it fires for noise.
alex: Agreed. Suggested Datadog monitor (prod):
```
avg(last_5m):100 * (sum:myapp.http.429{env:prod,org:*,rate_limit_reason:*}.as_count()/sum:myapp.http.requests{env:prod,org:*}.as_count()) by {org} > 5
```
maria: I’ll add a console card to show "quota remaining" and "burst window" per org so CS can see this without asking. I’ll mock in the console and link it to the quotas API.
sunil: Also pushing a platform change to add `rate_limit.reason` to 429 emitted metrics — that'll land behind a flag in the next hour.
jamie: Once root cause known, I’ll draft a short customer note: what happened, what we changed, and advise next steps (increase reserved capacity or adjust burst).
sam: done: increased burst for acme, monitoring 10m. Current 429 rate dropped to ~1.2% after bump. Will escalate to infra if it creeps back. :thumbsup:
ryan: Follow-up actions: alex to update monitor (split by reason), sunil to deploy telemetry flag, maria to add console card, jamie to prepare customer message. Assigning owners here — please update status in this thread.
alex: I’ll update the monitor in the next 30m.
sunil: Telemetry flag deploying now.
maria: UX mock in progress, will post link when ready.
jamie: Draft ready, will hold until we confirm final RCA.
ryan: Great work — keep this thread updated. If it resurfaces, escalate to incident channel. :rocket:
